results.summary_before: This design is a 4-neuron digital spiking neural network (SNN) inference engine with hard winner-take-all lateral inhibition. Each neuron accumulates a MAC of its bias, input currents, and synaptic weights, with programmable threshold, leak, and refractory parameters. It is SPI-configurable and provides spike outputs, winner ID, and status flags. It requires an SPI master for programming and an input pattern generator, with optional oscilloscope for spike capture.

results.summary_before: This design implements a digital desk clock that displays hours, minutes, and seconds in 24-hour format. It uses SPI to drive a MAX7219 7-segment display driver because there are not enough output pins to directly control six 7-segment displays. The time can be set using dedicated buttons for hours and minutes, with a fast/slow adjustment mode and a 12-hour mode option. The design requires an external MAX7219 module and a 32.768 kHz reference clock for accurate timekeeping.

results.summary_before: This design computes a 5-bit rolling average over 8 banks. It uses a shift register and a rolling sum trick to generate the average. Data is clocked in via i_data_clk and the 5-bit value is output on io_out[4:0]. It requires external GPIO connections to provide input and read the output.

results.summary_before: This is a Logisim demo showing how to use Logisim Evolution generated Verilog for TinyTapeout. It implements a 4-bit ring shift register with a single '1' cycling through it after reset. The design has four outputs that blink in sequence and requires a button for reset and LEDs or another display for the outputs. It serves as an educational example for using Logisim with TinyTapeout.

results.summary_before: This design implements a single fracturable 5-input lookup table (LUT) that can be configured via serial SRAM or FLASH frames. It receives 92-bit LUT configuration frames serially, four bits per cycle, and evaluates the LUT every 23 clock cycles. The last 283 LUT output values are stored on-chip to serve as inputs for subsequent LUTs, and the design includes two FPGA input pins and seven output pins plus a debug pin. Testing is described as tricky, and external serial memory is required for configuration.

results.summary_before: This design is a purely combinational 4-bit multiplier that takes two 4-bit numbers on its input pins and produces an 8-bit product on its output pins. It is implemented using AND gates and several adders, without any sequential logic. To use it, a user would apply the two operands via switches or other sources and read the binary result on LEDs. The project is a straightforward arithmetic building block and requires external hardware such as DIP switches and LEDs for input and output.
